subject: Mixed (Real Weightage)

questions.explanation: UV thickens the epidermis through stimulation of keratinocytes.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)
questions.subject: Fundamentals of Electro Therapy

questions.question: The second heart sound (S2) is caused by:

options.A: Closure of the mitral and tricuspid valves
options.D: Closure of the aortic and pulmonary valves

questions.explanation: S1 marks the start of systole; S3 is rapid ventricular filling (normal in children).
questions.sourceBook: A.K. Jain, Textbook of Physiology; Guyton & Hall, Textbook of Medical Physiology (chapter-level reference)
questions.subject: Physiology

questions.question: A therapist observes that a patient has an exaggerated heel strike on the left during ambulation activities. Which term is most consistent with heel strike using Rancho Los Amigos nomenclature?
questions.explanation: Rancho Los Amigos names the heel strike phase initial contact.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)
questions.sourceChapter: Cited reference: Joint Structure and Function/Norkin/3rd Ed./Pg. 443
questions.subject: Kinesio Therapeutics

questions.question: A therapist designs an exercise program for a patient rehabilitating from a lower extremity injury. The single most important factor in an exercise program designed to increase muscular strength is:

options.A: The recovery time between exercise sets
options.B: The number of repetitions per set
options.C: The duration of the exercise session

questions.explanation: Exercise intensity (load) is the most important variable for increasing strength.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)
questions.subject: Fundamentals of Exercise Therapy

questions.question: The National Rural Health Mission was launched in India in:
questions.explanation: Now subsumed under the National Health Mission.

questions.question: Complete aerobic oxidation of one molecule of glucose yields approximately:
questions.explanation: Older textbooks quote 36–38 ATP.
questions.sourceBook: U. Satyanarayana, Biochemistry; Harper's Illustrated Biochemistry (chapter-level reference)
questions.subject: Biochemistry

questions.question: Commonest degenerative joint disease is:
questions.explanation: Osteoarthritis is the commonest degenerative joint disease.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: Benzodiazepines act by:
questions.explanation: Flumazenil is the antagonist.
questions.sourceBook: K.D. Tripathi, Essentials of Medical Pharmacology (chapter-level reference)
questions.subject: Pharmacology

questions.question: Active repetitive exercises, usually of the ankles or wrist performed to maintain or improve circulation in the extremities are also known as:
questions.explanation: Pumping exercises of the ankles or wrists maintain circulation.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: A physical therapist examines a patient with multiple sclerosis. The therapist documents that the patient presents with dysdiadochokinesia. Which objective finding is most representative of dysdiadochokinesia?

options.A: Inability to perform rapid alternating movements
options.B: Inability to discriminate selected tactile input
options.D: Presence of involuntary, rhythmic, and oscillatory movements at rest

questions.explanation: Dysdiadochokinesia is inability to perform rapid alternating movements.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)
questions.sourceChapter: Cited reference: Physical Rehabilitation/O'Sullivan/4th Ed./ Pg. 740

questions.question: Which aquatic exercise would be the most effective in reducing tone in a patient with a spinal cord injury?

options.A: Slow passive movements of the neck and upper extremities with the patient floating in supine
options.B: Passive abduction and adduction of the upper extremities with the patient in short sitting
options.C: Approximation of the trunk with the patient floating in supine
options.D: Gentle rocking of the trunk with the patient in short sitting

questions.explanation: Slow passive movements while floating in warm water relax muscles and reduce tone.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Neurosciences

questions.question: A physical therapist examines a patient with unilateral lower extremity weakness. As the patient performs hip flexion in supine, the therapist helps the patient complete the full range of motion. This would best be described as:
questions.explanation: Helping the patient through the range is active-assisted exercise.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)
questions.subject: Fundamentals of Exercise Therapy

questions.question: A patient with a full-thickness burn over the entire anterior aspect of the neck is examined in physical therapy. The physical therapist must plan a treatment program based on the anticipation of a possible _______ contracture: 8
questions.explanation: A burn over the anterior neck tends to produce a flexion contracture.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in General Medical & Surgical Condition

questions.question: Which of the following does not have the blood supply?
questions.explanation: Articular cartilage is avascular and gets nutrition by diffusion from synovial fluid.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)
questions.subject: Anatomy

questions.question: A patient three weeks status post right total kneere placement complains of pain in the right calf. The patient's pain increases with ambulation and with quick passive range of motion into dorsiflexion. The patient's lower extremity is warm to touch. The most appropriate response would be to:

options.A: Disregard the findings as postoperative pain
options.D: Request a physician to rule out deep venous thrombosis

questions.explanation: Calf pain, warmth and pain on passive dorsiflexion after knee replacement suggest DVT and need medical evaluation.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in General Medical & Surgical Condition

questions.question: End-stage renal disease is defined as GFR below:
questions.explanation: Renal replacement therapy is needed.
questions.sourceBook: Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine; Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine (chapter-level reference)
questions.subject: Medicine

questions.question: A 16-year-old basketball player is anxious to return to athletic competition following rehabilitation from an Achilles tendon rupture. The athlete is objectively ready to return to competition, however continues to demonstrate a severe preoccupation with reinjury. The most appropriate response is the:

options.A: Allow the patient to return to basketball without restriction
options.B: Information patient that he should not participate in basketball this season
options.C: Design a functional progression for basketball which allows the patient to progress to higher level activities in a gradual fashion
options.D: Discuss other less demanding athletic activities with the patient

questions.explanation: A graded functional progression back to sport addresses fear of reinjury.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)
questions.sourceChapter: Cited reference: Essential of Orthopaedics & Applied Physiotherapy/ Jayant Joshi/1st Ed./Pg. 562-563

questions.question: Anterior dislocation of shoulder causes all except:
questions.explanation: Anterior shoulder dislocation does not cause hip bone fractures.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: Underweight in children is defined as weight-for-age below:

options.D: −2 SD of the WHO reference median

questions.explanation: Stunting: height-for-age <−2 SD; wasting: weight-for-height <−2 SD.

questions.question: The ankle–brachial pressure index in intermittent claudication is typically:

questions.question: A physical therapist examines a patient with lower extremity hypertonicity. All of the following could be used by the therapist to temporarily reduce tone except:
questions.explanation: Approximation facilitates tone; rocking, cold and sustained stretch reduce it.

questions.question: A patient diagnosed with low back pain is referred to physical therapy. During the initial examination the therapist ask if the patient has any formal diagnostic screening. The patient states that she had X-rays and a test where dye was injected into the spinal canal. This description most closely resembles:

options.D: Magnetic resonance imaging 147. Which clinical finding would you expect to see from a patient diagnosed with right-sided heart failure? A. Dyspnea B. Cough C. Dependent edema D. Orthopnea

questions.explanation: Injecting contrast dye into the spinal canal is myelography.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)
